To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the LFI-DPCL1 end-to-end test procedure, developed according to the ESA software engineering standards, is effective to validate the LFI Level 1 software; it allows to test the scientific processing of the raw data, reproducing the on-board processing; it allows to validate the housekeeping processing of raw data, injecting known parameters in the HK data; it allows to perform the verification of the LFI Level1 software in a systematic way, by testing the scientific and house keeping data
the Level 1 LFI-DPC has been successfully validated and that it is ready to process the real telemetry during the flight operations.

the end-to-end approach to the verification and validation of the Level 0-1 software has been successfully applied to the Planck-LF1 DPC; the tests have been designed and implemented following ESA Software Engineering Standards; the results of the tests are satisfactory and the software is ready for the flight.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a systematic approach to the end-to-end verification of a space instrument, and the application of this methodology to the LFI-DPc Level 1.
the validation of the Level 0-1 pipeline, the first step in the processing of Planck LFI raw data, which is responsible for the generation of the calibrated timelines.
the development of a systematic approach to the validation of the Level 0 and Level 1 software of a satellite mission.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the LFI Level 1 pipeline has been successfully verified and validated, and it is ready to be used by the DPC for the processing of the real telemetry data during the mission operations.
the Level 1 pipeline is fully compliant with the project requirements and the software is ready to be delivered to the LFI DPC.
the LFI Level 1 is ready for the start of the Planck flight operations and the subsequent science operations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Planck-Low Frequency Instrument Level 1 software is ready for the start of the flight operations.
the Level 1 pipeline has passed the verification and validation tests and the results are in agreement with the requirements.
the Planck L1 pipeline is now fully operational and the DPC is able to provide to the DPU a Level 1 data product ready for further processing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed approach can be used as a reference for other ESA projects, to ensure a high quality of the software development.
, in order to ensure the quality of a complex software, a systematic approach to the validation is essential.
a systematic approach is essential to the development and validation of the ground segment of a space mission.
